[P2] Complete quarantine handling before Jest's teardown deadline

The subprocess timeout equals the enclosing `afterEach` timeout of 180000 ms. If settlement stalls, Jest can time out the hook and start the next case before the subprocess exits and this function's catch block writes the quarantine file. The next case can therefore invoke the unsettled shared function. Give the subprocess a shorter deadline than the hook, with time for exit and quarantine handling, or mark the fixture unavailable synchronously before settlement and clear that state only on success. Add a stalled-subprocess regression that verifies subsequent invocations remain blocked.
